subject: Mid-cycle leadership briefing: re-scope OKRs & critical unblocks
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-cycle leadership briefing: re-scope OKRs & critical unblocks

Team —

Attached is a short briefing for our mid-cycle leadership readout and the QBR deck stub (QBR_brief_v1.pdf). High level: two production-facing OKRs are drifting and require either additional runway or a narrowed scope. I summarized options and the dependency map on slide 3.

Key signals:
- Serving throughput (OKR-Serve): behind plan — current blockers are scheduling & GPU availability for perf replay.
- Cost per token (OKR-Cost): trending worse due to unexpected tail latency and suboptimal batching on small-latency routes.

Proposed immediate moves (we need decisions by EOD Wed, Aug 12):
1) Narrow OKR-Serve acceptance criteria to 95th %-tile latency at peak vs full 99th‑tile target (Option A: partial scope, Option B: full scope with extra runway).
2) Shift a set of non-critical experiments out of Q3 to free capacity for perf replay (list in appendix).
3) Request infra priority for two tickets (INF-413, INF-421) for the next sprint; see perf_workplan.xlsx for proposed staffing and ETA windows.

Asks by role:
- Markus: decision on temporary reallocation of two backend engineers and approval for dedicated GPU slots for perf replay.
- Karthik: quick assessment of INF-413/INF-421 feasibility and minimal ETA to unblock.
- Kimberly/Product: pick the trimmed success criteria for OKR-Cost if we opt to narrow scope.
- Naomi: alignment on executive messaging and whether we escalate any SLA/credit talk to customer success.

Ive cc'd sam@clearcloud.ai because partner scheduling for the marketplace demo depends on whether we proceed with the full scope.

Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Head of Growth & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: QBR_brief_v1.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)]
[Attachment: perf_workplan.xlsx (xlsx, 540KB)]

Thanks Vanessa — reviewed the deck. I lean toward Option A for OKR-Serve (narrow acceptance to 95th) so we can guarantee delivery for Q3 without adding headcount.

Two quick notes:
- I will authorize reallocation of the two backend engineers for three weeks, provided infra confirms they can make the perf replay schedule without cascading impact.
- If infra says the GPU slot work will take >3 weeks, we need to consider a brief runway extension and call it out in QBR messaging.

- INF-413 (priority scheduling changes): we have a patch ready but need a dedicated test window; ETA for staging rollout is 6 business days after allocation.
- INF-421 (batching adjustments): small change but requires cross-model regression testing; ETA 9 business days.

I created two quick tickets and attached the INF-413-ticket.pdf with basic runbook & rollback plan. If Markus signs off on the two backend engineers and a 3-week priority slot, we can target a staging runway starting Mon Aug 17.

- Option 2: Keep cost target but move quality guardrails to an experiment track (not part of OKR delivery).

1) OKR-Serve: adopt Option A (narrow to 95th %-tile baseline). Markus approves reallocation of two backend engineers and GPU slots; infra to start staging work week of Aug 17 (Karthik to confirm schedule & tickets moved to In Progress).
2) OKR-Cost: Kimberly will take Option 1 (relax small-latency target). Kimberly to deliver updated acceptance criteria doc by EOD Wed, Aug 12 and I will fold it into slide 3.
3) Communications: Naomi will draft the exec note; markus to review.
4) Partners: Sam@clearcloud.ai — we'll update them that we are narrowing scope to secure the marketplace demo timeline; no customer-facing SLA changes expected today.

Owners & actions: 
- Karthik: INF-413 & INF-421 start dates and staging ETA (due by EOD Tue Aug 12).
- Kimberly: Updated acceptance criteria doc (due EOD Wed Aug 12).
- Naomi: Exec note draft (due EOD Wed Aug 12).
